title: Viniyoga of drupadād iva

words.gram: the mantra’s first words, quoted as a name

words.meaning: so-and-so (a blank: the seer is not named)
anuṣṭubh, the metre of four lines of eight syllables
Drupadā (the mantra’s deity, named from its first word)
in the smelling (holding the water to the nose)

words.role: what the mantra is used for

translation.literal: Of the mantra “drupadād iva”: so-and-so the seer, anuṣṭubh the metre, Drupadā the deity, the use in smelling.
translation.readable: Drupadād iva: seer — (not named), metre anuṣṭubh, deity Drupadā; used for holding the water to the nose.

sandhi_exceptions.note: The prayoga writes the visarga before the following vowel, the words left apart as separate phrases of the formula, instead of joining them.

meaning: A viniyoga is the statement said before a mantra of its seer (ṛṣi), its metre (chandas), its deity (devatā) and the use (viniyoga) it is put to. Here: drupadād iva muñcatu, recited while water held in the hand is brought to the nose and then thrown away (āghrāṇa). The witness leaves the seer blank with amuka, ‘so-and-so’, written in parentheses: it does not know or does not give his name. The commas of the witness mark the pauses between the parts; a word before a comma keeps its pausal form, so the comma is written with the word in the padaccheda.
in_the_rite: Step aghrana, before drupadād iva (M only).
